Each domain includes pattern tables with concrete examples such as PostgreSQL read replicas, Cassandra time-series ingestion, DynamoDB cart merge, and Debezium-fed search indexes. items.description: Follow a structured checklist that prevents common database design mistakes before writing any SQL or ORM code.
items.summary: Database Schema Designer helps developers create scalable, maintainable database schemas for SQL and NoSQL systems. It guides users through four phases: analysis (identify entities and access patterns), design (normalize to 3NF or embed/reference, define keys and constraints), optimize (indexing and denormalization strategies), and migrate (reversible, zero-downtime scripts). The tool covers normalization rules (1NF through 3NF), data type selection, foreign key strategies (CASCADE, RESTRICT, SET NULL), index optimization for query patterns, and migration best practices. Developers use it when starting new projects, retrofitting existing schemas, or evolving production databases while maintaining data integrity and performance. Generates complete SQL schemas from entity descriptions with proper primary/foreign keys and constraints Covers normalization (1NF-3NF), denormalization trade-offs, and OLTP vs OLAP access pattern design Provides indexing strategies grounded in column selectivity and composite index ordering
highlights: Generates complete SQL schemas from entity descriptions with proper primary/foreign keys and constraints
Covers normalization (1NF-3NF), denormalization trade-offs, and OLTP vs OLAP access pattern design

items.name: commit
items.author: getsentry
items.description: Generate consistent, conventional commit messages that follow Sentry standards every time they save or commit code changes.
items.summary: Commit is a Sentry agent skill that must run before any git commit so messages follow conventional commit format and engineering conventions. It requires checking the current branch and creating a feature branch when on main or master unless the user explicitly requests otherwise. The header format is type, optional scope, and imperative subject under 70 characters with types such as feat, fix, ref, perf, docs, test, build, ci, chore, style, meta, and license. Body text explains what and why in present tense without customer data, using real newlines instead of escaped sequences. Footers reference issues with Fixes or Refs patterns for GitHub, Sentry, or Linear tickets. AI-generated commits add a Co-Authored-By footer with the agent identity and avoid marketing phrases about AI in the subject or body. Examples cover simple fixes, features, refactors, breaking changes, and revert messages. Developers invoke it whenever an agent prepares a repository commit in Sentry projects.

Its four-step system covers a curiosity-driven landing page, a questionnaire that captures contact information first then asks scored category questions, a personalized results page with tier-specific dynamic content and CTAs, and sales and marketing automation segmented by score tier. Core psychology emphasizes dormant desires over active searchers, self-referential encoding, reciprocity, and gamified scoring that benchmarks 30-50% conversion versus 3-10% for traditional lead magnets. Results pages show overall and category scores, tier copy for low medium and high segments, optional PDF reports, and tier-appropriate next steps. Promotion spans ads, email, podcasts, and abandonment recovery, with ethical boundaries against bait-and-switch h.

items.name: langsmith-evaluator
items.author: langchain-ai
items.description: Stand up LangSmith evaluators, run functions, and evaluate() runs so agent outputs are scored before you ship changes.
items.summary: LangSmith Evaluator is a LangChain skill for building agent evaluation pipelines across three components: creating evaluators, defining run functions, and running evaluations locally or via uploaded evaluators. Offline evaluators attach to datasets with a (run, example) signature; online evaluators attach to projects with a (run) signature for production checks. The golden rule requires running the agent on sample inputs and inspecting actual output before writing evaluator logic. LLM-as-Judge evaluators use structured output; custom code evaluators handle trajectory validation and format checks. Each evaluator returns one metric only as score and comment. Python local evaluate() passes RunTree objects while uploaded evaluators receive dicts, so handlers must support both. Run functions capture outputs and optionally trajectories via LangGraph stream_mode debug with subgraphs. The langsmith CLI uploads code evaluators that auto-run on dataset experiments. Uploaded evaluators run in a sandbox with limited packages, so local evaluate() is preferred for development. Setup requires LANGSMITH_API_KEY and langsmith plus langchain-openai dependencies.

items.name: pixijs-scene-container
items.author: pixijs
items.description: Get precise, on-demand guidance for grouping, positioning, transforming, and managing display objects inside PixiJS v8 scene graphs.
items.summary: PixiJS Scene Container documents the v8 Container node used to build scene graph branches in PixiJS games and interactive apps. It covers constructor options such as sortableChildren, isRenderGroup, boundsArea, and origin versus pivot, plus addChild, removeChild, reparentChild, and zIndex sorting when sortableChildren is enabled. Transform guidance spans position, scale, rotation, alpha, tint, visible versus renderable, and coordinate conversion with getBounds, toGlobal, toLocal, and getGlobalPosition. The skill explains leaf versus container rules so Sprites and Graphics stay wrapped in Containers, documents childAdded and destroyed events, and shows onRender per-frame callbacks replacing v7 updateTransform. Common mistakes call out getBounds returning Bounds not Rectangle, cacheAsBitmap renamed to cacheAsTexture, and avoiding children on leaf objects. Use it when grouping sprites, layering UI, converting coordinates, or tearing down subtrees with destroy options in PixiJS v8 projects.
highlights: Documents v8 Container constructor options including isRenderGroup, sortableChildren, boundsArea, and origin.
Covers addChild, reparentChild, zIndex sorting, and coordinate conversion with toGlobal and toLocal.
Explains leaf objects must be wrapped in Containers; adding children to Sprites is deprecated.
getBounds returns Bounds in v8; use .rectangle for Rectangle-specific APIs.
onRender replaces v7 updateTransform for lightweight per-frame container updates.

items.name: release-it
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Systematically identify and mitigate stability anti-patterns that cause production outages before they impact users.
items.summary: release-it is a Wondelai agent skill applying Release It! production resilience patterns across stability anti-patterns, stability patterns, capacity planning, and deployment release decoupling. It scores systems 0-10 on production readiness and treats integration points as the primary outage source where slow responses, unbounded result sets, retry storms, and blocked threads cascade across services. Stability pattern guidance covers circuit breaker closed-open-half-open states, bulkhead pool isolation, connect and read timeouts with deadline propagation, retry with exponential backoff and jitter budgets, fail-fast handshaking, steady-state cleanup, and let-it-crash restarts. Capacity work includes load, stress, soak, and spike tests, Universal Scalability Law limits, and connection pool sizing from measured P99 concurrency plus headroom. Deployment guidance separates deploy from release with blue-green health gates, canary rollback on error thresholds, feature flags, expand-contract database migrations, and immutable infrastructure. Developers reach for it when investigating cascading failures, designing resilient microservices, planning chaos engineering, or setting health chec.
highlights: Scores production systems 0-10 across stability anti-patterns, patterns, capacity, and release readiness.
Documents circuit breaker, bulkhead, timeout propagation, and backoff-with-jitter retry budgets.
Covers load, stress, soak, and spike testing plus pool sizing from measured concurrency.
Separates deploy from release with blue-green gates, canary rollback, and feature flags.

items.name: pixijs-assets
items.author: pixijs
items.description: Preload game textures, sprites, and UI assets without freezing the main thread in PixiJS projects.
items.summary: The pixijs-assets skill documents PixiJS v8's unified Assets loader, resolver, and cache for textures, video, spritesheets, fonts, JSON, GIFs, and compressed GPU formats. It recommends Assets.init for basePath, texturePreference, and manifest-driven setups, then Assets.load for URLs, aliases, arrays, or UnresolvedAsset descriptors. A parser field forces loaders for extension-less CDN or API URLs, replacing deprecated loadParser. Reference files cover bundles, manifests, background loading, progress callbacks, caching, SVG modes, resolution detection, and per-asset data options distinct from LoadOptions retry strategy. Critical v8 rules forbid Texture.from for fetching, require object-form Assets.add, and call Assets.unload between levels to free GPU memory. Supported types span png, webp, avif, mp4, fnt, ktx2, basis, and gif with optional side-effect imports. Decision guidance maps single images, level bundles, loading bars, and memory budgets to the right reference workflow.
highlights: Assets.init, load, get, unload, and bundle patterns for PixiJS v8.
Parser field for extension-less URLs with full supported type table.
Separate LoadOptions retries versus per-asset data parser options.
Reference index for bundles, manifests, background load, and progress bars.
Critical fixes for Texture.from misuse and positional Assets.add removal.

items.summary: us-stock-analysis performs comprehensive US equity research by fetching live market data through web search and applying structured analytical frameworks. It supports four modes: basic stock info, fundamental analysis, technical analysis, and comprehensive reports combining all approaches. Data gathering targets current price and volume, financial statements, valuation metrics like P/E and EPS, analyst ratings, recent news, peer comparisons, and technical indicators such as RSI and MACD when available. Fundamental workflows pull multi-year revenue, earnings, cash flow, balance sheet metrics, profitability trends, competitive advantages, and valuation ratios compared to history and peers. Technical workflows cover chart patterns, support and resistance, and indicator interpretation. Search strategy uses ticker-specific queries, prefers recent quarterly data, and cites quality sources including Yahoo Finance, SEC filings, and TradingView. Output formats range from concise metric tables to full reports following bundled reference templates for fundamentals, metrics definitions, and report structure.
